items.title: Sc-smooth retractions

book.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.1 (preprint 2.1), p. 21 (preprint p. 18)
book.statement: For a tuple $(U, C, E)$, $U$ relatively open in the partial quadrant $C$ of $E$, an sc-smooth map $r : U \to U$ with $r \circ r = r$ is an *sc-smooth retraction* on $U$. After Definition 2.1.3 (preprint 2.3): for $x \in U_1$ the chain rule gives $Dr(r(x)) \circ Dr(x) = Dr(x)$, so for $x \in O_1$, $Dr(x)$ is a projection.

lean.statement: An *sc-smooth retraction* on $C$ is a set $U \subseteq E_0$ relatively open in the partial quadrant $C$ and a map $r : E_0 \to E_0$ (only its values on $U$ matter) with $r(U) \subseteq U$, $r$ sc-smooth on $U$ and $r(r(x)) = r(x)$ for $x \in U$. Its retract is $O = r(U)$; $O \subseteq U$, $O$ is the fixed-point set of $r$ in $U$, and for $x \in O_1$ the derivative satisfies $Dr(x) \circ Dr(x) = Dr(x)$.

diff: The retraction is a total map $E_0 \to E_0$ with $r(U) \subseteq U$ as a field; only its values on $U$ enter any statement.
The remark that $Dr(x)$ is a projection for $x \in O_1$ is `ScRetraction.scDeriv_comp_self`, by the chain rule applied to $r \circ r = r$.

items.title: Sc-smooth retracts

book.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.3 (preprint 2.3), p. 22 (preprint p. 18)
book.statement: A tuple $(O, C, E)$ is an *sc-smooth retract* if $O = r(U)$ for an sc-smooth retraction $r : U \to U$ on a relatively open subset $U$ of the partial quadrant $C$.

lean.statement: $(O, C, E)$ is an sc-smooth retract if $O$ is the retract $r(U)$ of some sc-smooth retraction on $C$. Every relatively open $U \subseteq C$ is a retract, with $r = \mathrm{id}$. A *local model* is a triple $(E, C, O)$ with $C$ a partial quadrant and $(O, C, E)$ a retract.

diff: As in the text. The local model packages the triple used by M-polyfold charts.

items.title: Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4): the tangent of a retract does not depend on the retraction

book.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4), p. 26 (preprint p. 19)
book.statement: If $r : U \to U$ and $r' : U' \to U'$ are sc-smooth retractions on relatively open subsets of $C$ with $r(U) = r'(U') = O$, then $Tr(TU) = Tr'(TU')$.

lean.statement: For sc-smooth retractions $r$ on $U$ and $r'$ on $U'$ (both relatively open in $C$) with the same retract, $Tr(TU) = Tr'(TU')$. More precisely, $r(U) \subseteq r'(U')$ already gives $r' \circ r = r$ on $U$ and $Tr(TU) \subseteq Tr'(TU')$. $TO = Tr(TU)$ is the fixed-point set of $Tr$ in $TU$.

diff: As in the text. The inclusion is proved under the weaker hypothesis $r(U) \subseteq r'(U')$ and applied twice.
The text's step \"$Tr'(x, h) = (x, h)$\" is the fixed-point description of $Tr(TU)$, proved separately (`ScRetraction.mem_tangent_iff`).

items.title: Definition 2.1.12 (preprint 2.5): the tangent $TO$ of a retract

book.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.12 (preprint 2.5), p. 26 (preprint p. 19)
book.statement: The tangent of $(O, C, E)$ is $T(O, C, E) = (TO, TC, TE)$ with $TC = C^1 \oplus E$, $TE = E^1 \oplus E$ and $TO := Tr(TU)$ for any retraction $r$ onto $O$; explicitly $TO = \{(r(x), Dr(x)h) : x \in U_1, h \in E\}$. Definition 2.3.12 (preprint 2.17): for $x \in O_1$, $T_xO = p^{-1}(x)$, the image of the projection $Dr(x)$.

lean.statement: $TO \subseteq E_1 \times E_0$ is $Tr(TU)$ for a chosen retraction onto $O$, and equals $Tr'(TU')$ for every other one; $TO = \{(r(x), Dr(x)h) : x \in U_1, h \in E_0\}$, and for $x \in O_1$, $(x, h) \in TO$ iff $h \in Dr(x)(E_0)$. The fibre $T_xO = \{h : (x, h) \in TO\}$ is the range of $Dr(x)$, a closed subspace of $E_0$.

diff: `retractTangent E C O` is defined for every set $O$ (empty when $O$ is not a retract), by a choice of retraction; Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4) makes the choice irrelevant (`retractTangent_eq`).
That $TC$ is a partial quadrant in $TE$ and $TU$ relatively open in it is V2.8 (and V1.36).

items.title: Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6): sc-smoothness on a retract is independent of the retraction

book.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6), p. 27 (preprint p. 20)
book.statement: Let $f : O \to O'$ and $r : U \to U$, $s : V \to V$ two retractions onto $O$. (1) $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth iff $f \circ s$ is. (2) If so, $T(f \circ r) = T(f \circ s)$ on $TO$. (3) $T(f \circ r)$ maps $TO$ into $TO'$.

lean.statement: For retractions $r$, $s$ onto the same $O$: (1) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth on $U$ then $f \circ s$ is sc-smooth on $V$; (2) then $T(f \circ r) = T(f \circ s)$ on $Tr(TU)$; (3) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth and $f$ maps $O$ into the retract $O' = r'(U')$, then $T(f \circ r)$ maps $Tr(TU)$ into $Tr'(TU')$.

diff: (1) is stated in one direction; the other is the same theorem with $r$ and $s$ exchanged.
(3) assumes $f(O) \subseteq O'$, which the text's \"$f : O \to O'$\" contains.

items.title: Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7): sc-smooth maps between retracts and the tangent map

book.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7), pp. 27–28 (preprint pp. 20–21)
book.statement: $f : O \to O'$ is *sc-smooth* if $f \circ r : U \to E'$ is sc-smooth for a retraction $r$ onto $O$; $Tf := T(f \circ r)|_{TO}$, which maps $TO$ into $TO'$ and does not depend on $r$. For $o \in O_1$, $Tf(o) : T_oO \to T_{f(o)}O'$ is the linearization.

lean.statement: $f : E_0 \to E'_0$ is sc-smooth between the retracts $(O, C, E)$ and $(O', C', E')$ if $f(O) \subseteq O'$ and $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth on $U$ for *every* retraction $r$ onto $O$; for an actual retract this is equivalent to the text's \"for one $r$\". $Tf$ is $T(f \circ r)$ for a chosen $r$; on $TO$ it equals $T(f \circ r)$ for every $r$ onto $O$, maps $TO$ into $TO'$, and $Tf(x, h) = (f(x), D(f \circ r)(x)h)$. Sc-smooth maps between retracts are continuous on $O$ and preserve the levels.

diff: The definition quantifies over all retractions onto $O$ and includes $f(O) \subseteq O'$; `isScSmoothRetractMap_iff_exists` recovers the text's form for a retract.
The linearization $Tf(o)$ is the second component of $Tf(o, \cdot)$; it is not given a separate name.

items.title: Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8): the chain rule for retracts

book.label: §2.1, Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8), p. 28 (preprint p. 21)
book.statement: If $f : O \to O'$ and $g : O' \to O''$ are sc-smooth maps between sc-smooth retracts, then $g \circ f$ is sc-smooth and $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$ (the text writes $(O'', C', E'')$ for $(O'', C'', E'')$).

lean.statement: Let $(O, C, E)$ and $(O', C', E')$ be retracts, $f$ sc-smooth $(O, C, E) \to (O', C', E')$ and $g$ sc-smooth $(O', C', E') \to (O'', C'', E'')$. Then $g \circ f$ is sc-smooth and $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$ on $TO$. The identity, a retraction $U \to O$ and the inclusion $O \to U$ are sc-smooth, and sc-smoothness depends only on $f|_O$.

diff: The source and middle sets are assumed to be retracts (the text's standing hypothesis); $O''$ need not be.

The text gives no proof (\"follows from Theorem 1.21\"); the proof writes $(g \circ f) \circ r = (g \circ r') \circ (f \circ r)$ on $U$, which uses $r' \circ f \circ r = f \circ r$, and applies Theorem 1.3.1 (preprint 1.21).

items.title: The tangent functor on retracts

book.label: §2.1, after Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8) and Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9), pp. 27–30 (preprint pp. 21–22)
book.statement: $T$ is a functor $\mathcal R \to \mathcal R$: $(TO, TC, TE)$ is again a retract, $Tf : (TO, TC, TE) \to (TO', TC', TE')$, $Tf(x, h) = (f(x), Df(x)h)$, and $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$. If $r$ is a retraction, $Tr : TU \to TU$ is a (bundle) retraction.

lean.statement: $TC$ is a partial quadrant in $TE$ and $TU$ is relatively open in $TC$; $Tr : TU \to TU$ is an sc-smooth retraction with image $TO$, so $(TO, TC, TE)$ is an sc-smooth retract. If $f$ is sc-smooth between retracts, so is $Tf : (TO, TC, TE) \to (TO', TC', TE')$; $T(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id}$ on $TO$, and the chain rule is V2.7. $T(O \cap W) = TO \cap (W_1 \times E_0)$ for $W$ open, and $Tf$ computed on $O \cap W$ is $Tf$ computed on $O$.

diff: The functor is stated as the two facts that make it one: $T$ sends retracts to retracts and sc-smooth maps to sc-smooth maps; functoriality is Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8).

The bundle structure of $TO \to O^1$ is V2.92 ($Tr$ a bundle retraction covering $r^1$, $Tf$ a bundle map; G.5, formalized since); Definition 2.1.16's (preprint 2.9) category $\mathcal{BR}$ is not formalized; the fibrewise linearity of $Tf$ is the linearity of the derivative.
The locality of $Tf$ under restriction to open subsets, used silently in Definitions 2.3.12–2.3.14 (preprint 2.17–2.18), is proved here.

items.title: Proposition 2.3.1 (preprint 2.10): open subsets and images of retractions are retracts

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Proposition 2.3.1 (preprint 2.10), p. 33 (preprint p. 23)
book.statement: (1) An open subset $O'$ of a retract $O$ is a retract. (2) If $V \subseteq O$ is open and $s : V \to V$ is sc-smooth with $s \circ s = s$, then $s(V)$ is a retract.

lean.statement: (1) If $(O, C, E)$ is a retract and $W \subseteq E_0$ is open, $(O \cap W, C, E)$ is a retract, with the restriction of $r$ to $U \cap r^{-1}(W)$. (2) If $(V, C, E)$ is a retract and $s$ is sc-smooth $(V, C, E) \to (V, C, E)$ with $s \circ s = s$ on $V$, then $(s(V), C, E)$ is a retract, with the retraction $s \circ r$. Sc-smooth maps between retracts restrict to open subsets of the source, and sc-smoothness between retracts is a local property.

diff: \"An open subset $O'$ of $O$\" is written $O \cap W$ with $W$ open in $E_0$ (the subspace topology).
In (2), $V$ is a retract by (1) in the text; here it is assumed to be one, which is how (2) is applied.
The locality of sc-smoothness between retracts is not in the text; Definitions 2.3.4–2.3.8 (preprint 2.13–2.14) need it (V2.12).

items.title: Definition 2.3.2 (preprint 2.11): charts and their compatibility

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.2 (preprint 2.11), pp. 34 ff. (preprint pp. 23–24)
book.statement: A chart around $x$ in a space $X$ is $(V, \varphi, (O, C, E))$ with $V$ an open neighbourhood of $x$, $(O, C, E)$ an sc-smooth retract and $\varphi : V \to O$ a homeomorphism. Two charts are sc-smoothly compatible if $\psi \circ \varphi^{-1} : \varphi(V \cap V') \to \psi(V \cap V')$ and its inverse are sc-smooth (Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7)); $\varphi(V \cap V')$ is a retract by Proposition 2.3.1(1) (preprint 2.10).

lean.statement: A chart on $X$ is a local model $(O, C, E)$ and a partial equivalence $\varphi : X \rightharpoonup E_0$ with open source $V$, target $O$, continuous on $V$ with inverse continuous on $O$. The overlap $\varphi(V \cap V')$ is a retract; two charts are compatible if $\psi \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth from $(\varphi(V \cap V'), C, E)$ to $(\psi(V \cap V'), C', E')$ and $\varphi \circ \psi^{-1}$ back. A chart is compatible with itself and with its restrictions; compatibility is local: two charts compatible with every chart of a family covering $V \cap V'$ are compatible.

diff: The chart is a partial equivalence $X \rightharpoonup E_0$; its inverse is a total function whose values off $O$ do not matter.
`MChart.compatible_of_locally` (chain rule plus locality) is not in the text; it makes the maximal atlas of V2.12 an atlas.

items.title: Definition 2.3.3 (preprint 2.12): sc-smooth atlases and their equivalence

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.3 (preprint 2.12), p. 35 (preprint p. 24)
book.statement: An sc-smooth atlas is a set of pairwise compatible charts covering $X$; two atlases are equivalent if their union is an atlas.

lean.statement: An atlas is a set of pairwise compatible charts whose sources cover $X$. Two atlases are equivalent iff their union is an atlas iff every chart of one is compatible with every chart of the other; the relation is an equivalence relation.

diff: As in the text. Transitivity, which the “equivalence class” of Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13) presupposes without comment, is proved from the locality of compatibility (`MAtlas.Equiv.trans`; Findings, Chapter 2, item 41); the maximal atlas of V2.12 had made it unnecessary for the later notions. Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13): M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13), p. 35 (preprint p. 24)
book.statement: An M-polyfold is a Hausdorff paracompact topological space with an equivalence class of sc-smooth atlases.

lean.statement: An M-polyfold structure on a Hausdorff paracompact space $X$ is an sc-smooth atlas. Its *charts* are all charts compatible with that atlas (the maximal atlas); any two of them are compatible, restrictions of charts are charts, every point lies in a chart, and equivalent atlases have the same charts. A nonempty retract $(O, C, E)$ is an M-polyfold with the single chart $\mathrm{id}$.

diff: An equivalence class of atlases is represented by one atlas; every later notion is defined through the maximal atlas `IsChart`, which depends only on the class (`isChart_congr`).
That charts compatible with an atlas are compatible with each other needs the locality of compatibility (V2.10); the text does not discuss it.

items.title: Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14): sc-smooth maps between M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14), p. 37 (preprint p. 24)
book.statement: $f : X \to Y$ is sc-smooth if for charts $\varphi$ around $x$ and $\varphi'$ around $f(x)$ with $f(V) \subseteq V'$, $\varphi' \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1} : O \to O'$ is sc-smooth (Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7)); \"the definition does not depend on the choice of charts\".

lean.statement: $f$ is sc-smooth on an open $U \subseteq X$ if it is continuous on $U$ and for all charts $\varphi$ of $X$, $\psi$ of $Y$ and every open $V \subseteq U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ with $f(V) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\psi$, $\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth from $(\varphi(V), C, E)$ into $(O', C', E')$; sc-smooth means sc-smooth on $X$. It suffices to check one pair of charts around each point (the text's independence of charts). The identity is sc-smooth and compositions of sc-smooth maps are sc-smooth.

diff: Continuity of $f$ is a field: the text's charts with $f(V) \subseteq V'$ exist around every point only if $f$ is continuous.
The definition quantifies over all charts and all open $V$; `IsScSmoothOn.of_exists_charts` is the text's remark that one pair of charts per point suffices.
Maps on open subsets are included because germs and sub-M-polyfolds need them.

items.title: The filtration $X_m$ of an M-polyfold

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), after Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14), preprint p. 25
book.statement: $x$ is on level $m$ if $\varphi(x) \in O_m$ for a chart around $x$ (\"independent of the choice of a chart\"); $X_m$ is the set of such points, topologized by the basis of sets $\varphi^{-1}(W)$, $W$ open in $O_m$; $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset \cdots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap X_m$.

lean.statement: $X_m$ is the set of $x$ with $\varphi(x) \in \iota_m(E_m)$ for some chart $\varphi$ around $x$, and then for every chart around $x$. $X_0 = X$, $X_{m+1} \subseteq X_m$, $X_\infty = \bigcap_m X_m$. $X_m$ carries the topology generated by the sets $\{x \in V : \varphi(x) \in W\}$, $W$ open in $E_m$; with it the inclusion $X_m \to X$ is continuous, $X_m$ is Hausdorff, and $x \mapsto \varphi(x)$ embeds $V_m = V \cap X_m$ into $E_m$.

diff: The topology is the one *generated* by the text's family; that the family is a basis (closed under finite intersections) is not needed and not proved.
\"$\varphi : V_m \to O_m$ is a homeomorphism\" is `MPolyfold.isEmbedding_levelLift`.

items.title: Lemma 2.3.9 (preprint 2.15): the inclusions $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ are continuous

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Lemma 2.3.9 (preprint 2.15), p. 37 (preprint p. 25)
book.statement: The inclusion $i : X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is continuous for every $m \ge 0$.

lean.statement: For every $m$, the inclusion $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is continuous for the topologies of V2.14.

diff: As in the text: the preimage of a generating set $\varphi^{-1}(W)$ is the generating set $\varphi^{-1}(\mathrm{incl}_m^{-1}(W))$.

items.title: The level $X^1$ is an M-polyfold

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), after Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14), preprint p. 25
book.statement: $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$ is a chart on $X_m$; any two such charts are sc-smoothly compatible, and they form an atlas on $X_m$.

lean.statement: For every $m$, the identity of points is a homeomorphism $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$, and the level-$m$ lift of the level chart $\varphi^1$ is the level-$(m+1)$ lift of $\varphi$, so each iterate $(X^1)^1 \cdots$ is $X_m$ with its topology and charts (V2.93). For $m = 1$: a retraction $r$ on $U$ restricts to an sc-smooth retraction of $U^1 \subseteq C^1 \subseteq E^1$ with retract $O^1$, and an sc-smooth map between retracts induces an sc-smooth map $O^1 \to O'^1$. For every chart $\varphi$ of $X$, $(V_1, \varphi, (O^1, C^1, E^1))$ is a chart of $X_1$; any two are compatible; they form an atlas, and with it $X_1$ is an M-polyfold $X^1$ (its paracompactness is Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16), V2.17).

diff: Proved in full in V2.93; the narrower form first recorded here is kept (`MPolyfold.shift`, $m = 1$).

Only $X_1$ is made an M-polyfold; $X_m$ for $m \ge 2$ is reached as the iterate $(X^1)^1 \cdots$. Its points are those of $X_m$: $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (`MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff`, fourth addendum of this page); its topology and charts are those of $X_m$ (V2.14) by V2.93 (G.6, closed).
The text's \"by Proposition 1.17\" is `IsScSmoothRetractMap.shift`, Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for retracts.
`MPolyfold.shift` takes $X_1$ paracompact as an instance argument, which Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) now supplies (`MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_level`).

items.title: Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16): $X$, $X_m$ and $X_\infty$ are metrizable

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16), p. 37 (preprint p. 25) (proof §2.7.2 (preprint §2.6.2), pp. 71–76 (preprint pp. 56–58))
book.statement: For every $m \ge 0$ the space $X_m$ is metrizable, in particular paracompact; $X_\infty$ is metrizable. The proof uses Smirnov's theorem (2.55), Lemma 2.7.3 (preprint 2.56) and Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57).

lean.statement: For an M-polyfold $X$: $X$ is metrizable; every level $X_m$ (topology of V2.14) is metrizable and paracompact; $X_\infty$, with the initial topology of the inclusions $X_\infty \to X_m$, is metrizable. Every subset of $X$, in particular every sub-M-polyfold, is paracompact.

diff: No hypothesis is added. The text's route needs $X_m$ regular for Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57) and does not check it; the formal proof avoids Lemma 2.7.3 (preprint 2.56) and Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57) altogether.

Proof: a partition of unity of the paracompact Hausdorff $X$, subordinate to the chart domains and pulled back to $X_m$ along the continuous inclusion, gives an explicit metric (`metrizableSpace_of_pullback`); paracompactness follows by Stone's theorem.
The text never defines the topology of $X_\infty$; it is taken to be the initial topology of the inclusions, which is what the text's metric $\sum 2^{-m} d_m/(1 + d_m)$ induces.

items.title: Definition 2.3.12 (preprint 2.17): tangent vectors in a chart

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.12 (preprint 2.17), pp. 38–39 (preprint pp. 25–26)
book.statement: For $x \in O_1$, $T_xO = p^{-1}(x)$, the image of $Dr(x)$. Tuples $(x, V, \varphi, (O, C, E), h)$ with $x \in X_1$, $\varphi$ a chart around $x$ and $h \in T_{\varphi(x)}O$ are equivalent, $(x, \varphi, h) \sim (x', \psi, h')$, if $x = x'$ and $T(\varphi \circ \psi^{-1})(\psi(x))h' = h$.

lean.statement: A tangent tuple is $(x, \varphi, h)$ with $x \in X_1$, $\varphi$ a chart of the structure around $x$ and $(\varphi(x), h) \in TO$. Its transport to another chart $\psi$ around $x$ is $T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})(\varphi(x), h)$, computed on the overlap retract; transporting to $\varphi$ itself does nothing, transports land in $TO'$ over $\psi(x)$, and transporting to $\psi$ and then to $\chi$ is transporting to $\chi$. Two tuples are equivalent if their points agree and the transport of the first to the chart of the second is the second; this is an equivalence relation.

diff: The text does not check that the relation is an equivalence relation; it is, by the chain rule on the triple overlap and the locality of $Tf$ (`TangentPre.transport_transport`).
The relation is written with the transport in the direction $\varphi \to \psi$, $T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})(\varphi(x), h) = (\psi(x), h')$; it is the text's relation read from the other side.

items.title: Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18): the tangent space $TX$

book.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18), pp. 39 ff. (preprint pp. 26–27)
book.statement: $TX$ is the set of equivalence classes $[(x, \varphi, h)]$, $T_xX$ the classes over $x \in X_1$, a vector space; $TV$ is the set of classes over $V$ and $T\varphi : TV \to TO$, $[(x, \varphi, h)] \mapsto (\varphi(x), h)$, is linear on fibres. $TX$ is topologized by the sets $(T\varphi)^{-1}(W)$, $W$ open in $TO$.

lean.statement: $TX$ is the quotient of the tangent tuples by the equivalence of V2.18, with the projection $p : TX \to X_1$ and the fibres $T_xX = p^{-1}(x)$. For a chart $\varphi$, $TV = p^{-1}(V_1)$ and $T\varphi : TV \to TO$ sends a class to its transport to $\varphi$; $T\varphi[(x, \varphi, h)] = (\varphi(x), h)$, $T\varphi$ is injective on $TV$ with inverse $a \mapsto [(\varphi^{-1}(a), \varphi, a_2)]$, and $T\psi \circ (T\varphi)^{-1} = T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ on $T(\varphi(V \cap V'))$. The topology is generated by the sets $\{\alpha \in TV : T\varphi(\alpha) \in W\}$. $T_xX$ is a vector space, transported along one chart, and **for every chart** $\varphi$ around $x$, $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_{\varphi(x)}O$ is a linear isomorphism (`tangentFiberLinearEquiv`), with $\lambda[(x, \varphi, h_1)] + \mu[(x, \varphi, h_2)] = [(x, \varphi, \lambda h_1 + \mu h_2)]$ (`definition_2_3_14_2021`) and a homeomorphism onto the Banach space $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ (`tangentFiberContinuousLinearEquiv`); the fibre transitions are restrictions of $D(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})(\varphi(x))$. At a smooth $x$, $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ is an sc-subspace of $E$ and the transitions preserve the levels, so $T_xX$ is an sc-Banach space through any chart.

diff: Updated (2026-11-09): the vector space structure of $T_xX$, its Banach structure through every chart and its sc-structure at smooth points are formalized (`Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear.lean`; gap G.7 closed); the chart independence that the text leaves to the reader is the linearity of the fibre transitions. items.title: Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34): tame retractions and tame retracts

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34), pp. 53–54 (preprint pp. 39–40)
book.statement: An sc-smooth retraction $r : U \to U$ is tame if (1) $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$ on $U$ and (2) at every smooth $x \in O$ there is an sc-subspace $A \subset E_x$ with $E = T_xO \oplus A$. A tame retract is the image of a tame retraction.

lean.statement: $r$ is tame for the presentation $T$ if (1) $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$ for $x \in U$ and (2) for every smooth $x \in O_1$ there is $A \le E_x$ with $E = Dr(x)E \oplus A$ an sc-splitting (both summands sc-subspaces, complementary on every level). $r$ is tame if it is tame for every presentation of $C$, equivalently for one; a tame retract is the retract of a tame retraction. diff: `IsTame` asks tameness for every presentation of $C$; tameness for one presentation implies it (`IsTameWith.isTame`, from the independence of $E_x$), so the definition is the text's. The theorems of §2.5 (preprint §2.4) assume tameness for the presentation they compute in.

\"$E = T_xO \oplus A$\" is an sc-splitting, as an sc-complement must be.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35): $(1 - Dr(x))E \subseteq E_x$

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$ and $x \in O_1$ smooth. Then $(1 - Dr(x))E \le E_x$ and $E = Dr(x)E \oplus (1 - Dr(x))E$ is an sc-splitting. In coordinates, $\lambda_j \circ Dr(x) = \lambda_j$ for $j \in I(x)$.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36): $d_O = d_C$, $T^R_xO$ an sc-subspace, $C_xO$ a partial quadrant

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36), p. 56 (preprint p. 41)
book.statement: For a tame retract and smooth $x$: $T^R_xO$ has codimension $d_O(x)$, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x)$ (13), and $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$; for every $x \in O$, $d_O(x) = d_C(x)$ (14).

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$. (13) At a smooth $x \in O_1$: $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x) = d_C(x)$; moreover $T_xO$ and $T^R_xO$ are sc-subspaces of $E$, and $C_xO = T_xO \cap C_x$ is a partial quadrant in the sc-Banach space $T_xO$ (with the sc-structure induced from $E$). More generally, a chart $\varphi$ of any M-polyfold whose model is a tame retract realizes the degeneracy index: $d_X(y) = d_C(\varphi(y))$ for every $y$ in its domain.

diff: (13) and (14) as in the text; the general form for charts of any M-polyfold is what Proposition 2.5.14's (preprint 2.42) \"$d_V(y) = d_X(y)$\" needs.
The approximants $r(a, w_j)$, $w_j \in W_\infty$, are taken through the presentation (`exists_tendsto_smooth_degIndexWith`).

The text deduces "$C_xO$ is a partial quadrant" from the equality case of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31) (G.11; since proved without the equality, V2.33); here it is proved directly. The smooth vectors $\hat e_j = Dr(x)T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)$ satisfy $\lambda_{i_k}(\hat e_j) = \delta_{jk}$ by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35), and $v \mapsto ((\lambda_{i_j}v)_j, v - \sum_j \lambda_{i_j}(v)\hat e_j)$ is an sc-isomorphism $T_xO \cong \mathbb R^d \oplus T^R_xO$ carrying $C_xO$ onto $[0, \infty)^d \oplus T^R_xO$ (`splitIso`).

The text calls $T^R_xO$ a Banach space; it is proved to be an sc-subspace (the exposition's Lemma 3.A (1) in this case), which the sc-isomorphism needs: $Dr(x)T^{-1}(a, w')$, $w' \in W_\infty$, are smooth points of $T^R_xO$ converging to $u$ on level $m$. Both the sc-subspace property of $T^R_xO$ and the partial quadrant hold without tameness (V2.33); what tameness adds is that the quadrant has dimension $d_O(x) = d_C(x)$. items.title: Definition 2.5.10 (preprint 2.39): faces and face-structured M-polyfolds

items.title: Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40): faces of a tame retract

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40), p. 59 (preprint p. 43)
book.statement: For a tame retract $(O, C, E)$, the faces of $O$ are the connected components of the sets $f \cap O$, $f$ an extended face; the components of $f \cap O$ and $f' \cap O$ through $x$ agree iff $f = f'$.

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$, and call a face of the retract a set $\overline{\hat F} \cap O$, $\hat F$ a connected component of $S = \{z \in O : d_C(z) = 1\}$. Then $G$ is a face iff $G$ is the connected component of $f_i \cap O$ through some $e \in O$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$. For $x \in O$ with $\lambda_i(x) = 0$, if the components of $f_i \cap O$ and $f_j \cap O$ through $x$ coincide then $i = j$. These are the faces of the M-polyfold $O$.

diff: Extended faces are the coordinate hyperplanes of a presentation; faces are handled in $E_0$ and transferred to the M-polyfold $O$ by `isFace_toMPolyfold_iff` (using $d_O = d_C$, V2.42).
The text's proof is a sketch; the formal proof follows the exposition (Lemma 4.C, V2.45).

items.title: Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41): a tame retract is face-structured

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41), p. 59 (preprint p. 44)
book.statement: If $(O, C, E)$ is a tame retract, every $x \in O$ lies in precisely $d_O(x)$ faces.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42): local face count in a tame M-polyfold

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42), p. 60 (preprint p. 44)
book.statement: In a tame M-polyfold every $x$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ such that each $y \in V$ lies in precisely $d_X(y)$ faces of $V$ and $d_V(y) = d_X(y)$; globally $x$ lies in at most $d_X(x)$ faces.

lean.statement: Let $X$ be tame and $x \in X$. There is a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ around $x$ with tame model such that $d_X(y) = d_C(\varphi(y))$ and $d_O(\varphi(y)) = d_X(y)$ for all $y \in V$, and the M-polyfold $O$ is face-structured. Globally, $x$ lies in at most $d_X(x)$ faces of $X$.

diff: The neighbourhood $V$ is represented by the M-polyfold $O$ it is sc-diffeomorphic to through $\varphi$; its faces are those of $O$.
\"$d_V(y) = d_X(y)$\" uses that a tame chart realizes $d_X$ (V2.42), which the text does not say.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43): faces of a tame retract are tame sub-M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43), pp. 61–62 (preprint pp. 44–45)
book.statement: For a tame retraction $r$ onto $O$ and a face $F$ of $O$: there are an open neighbourhood $V^*$ of $F$ in $U$ and an sc-smooth retraction $s : V^* \to V^*$ onto $F$; $s$ restricted to $V = O \cap V^*$ makes $F$ a sub-M-polyfold of $O$. $F$ is tame and $d_F(x) = d_O(x) - 1$ for $x \in F$.

lean.statement: Let $r$ be tame for $T$ and $F$ a face of the retract, $F \subseteq f_i$. (a) There is an sc-smooth retraction $S$ on $U^* \subseteq U$, relatively open in $C$ with $F \subseteq U^*$, with retract $F$ and $S = r \circ P_i$, $P_i$ the sc-projection onto $f_i$; every face of the M-polyfold $O$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $O$. (b) With the sc-operators $\iota : \mathbb R^k \oplus W \to f_i$ (insert a zero coordinate) and $\pi : E \to \mathbb R^k \oplus W$ (delete it), $r' = \pi \circ r \circ \iota$ on $\iota^{-1}(U^*)$ is a tame retraction of $[0, \infty)^k \oplus W$ onto $\pi(F)$, and $d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1 = d_C(y)$ on $F$. (c) A face $F$ of a tame retract $O$, with its sub-M-polyfold structure, is a tame M-polyfold and $d_F(x) + 1 = d_O(x)$ for $x \in F$.

diff: The text's model $(F, C \cap f_1, f_1)$ uses the sc-subspace $f_1$; here the extended face is modelled on $\mathbb R^k \oplus W$ through $\iota$, $\pi$, and the retraction is $\pi \circ r \circ \iota$ rather than $r|_{U^* \cap f_1}$ (they correspond under $\iota$). Tameness (2) of $r'$ is proved with the complement $(1 - Dr'(x))E'$, by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) for $r$, not by intersecting with $f_1$.

$U^*$ is the union of the balls $B_e$ intersected with their preimages under $P_i$, because $P_i$ need not be norm-decreasing for the norm of $E_0$ (the exposition's \"$|P_1z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0$\" is false in general).
\"$r(0, b_2, \dots, b_k, v)$ has the first coordinate vanishing\" is the local structure lemma (V2.45). $d_F = d_O - 1$ is stated as $d_F + 1 = d_O$; $F$ is paracompact because faces are closed.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44): local faces and their intersections are tame

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44), p. 62 (preprint p. 46)
book.statement: In a tame M-polyfold every point $x$ has $d_X(x)$ local faces containing $x$; they are tame M-polyfolds with $d_F(x) = d_X(x) - 1$. The intersection $F^\sigma$ of the local faces of $\sigma \subseteq \mathcal F_x$ is a tame M-polyfold of codimension $\#\sigma$ with $d_{F^\sigma}(x) = d_X(x) - \#\sigma$ (stated without proof).

lean.statement: Let $X$ be tame and $x \in X$. There is a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ of the structure around $x$, with a tame retraction onto $O$, such that the point $\varphi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$, and every face $F$ of $O$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $O$ which, with its induced structure, is tame, with $d_F(\varphi(x)) + 1 = d_X(x)$ when $\varphi(x) \in F$. For every set $\sigma$ of face germs at $x$, i.e. $\sigma \subseteq I(\varphi(x))$, there are pairwise distinct faces $F_i \ni \varphi(x)$ of the retract ($i \in \sigma$, $F_i$ in the $i$-th coordinate hyperplane) and an open $B \ni \varphi(x)$ such that $A = \{y \in V : \varphi(y) \in B,\ \varphi(y) \in F_i\ \forall i \in \sigma\}$ (whose germ at $x$ is $F^\sigma_x$) is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$, tame with its induced structure, and $d_A(y) + \#\sigma = d_X(y)$ for all $y \in A$.

items.title: Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45): interiors of faces and faces of face-structured M-polyfolds

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45), p. 62 (preprint p. 46)
book.statement: The interior of a face $F$ in a tame M-polyfold is an sc-smooth sub-M-polyfold of $X$. items.title: Products of M-polyfolds (exposition Lemma 4.D)

book.statement: Used without statement in Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46): $X \times Y$ is an M-polyfold (with the product charts) and $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$.

items.title: Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46): fibred products

book.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46), pp. 63–64 (preprint pp. 46–47)
book.statement: For a local sc-diffeomorphism $f : X \to Z$ and an sc-smooth $g : Y \to Z$, $X {}_f\times_g Y$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X \times Y$; if $Y$ is tame, so is the fibred product, with $d(x, y) = d_Y(y)$; with both maps local sc-diffeomorphisms and both spaces tame, $d = \frac12 d_{X \times Y} = d_X(x) = d_Y(y)$.

lean.statement: Let $f : X \to Z$ be a local sc-diffeomorphism (each point has an open neighbourhood mapped sc-diffeomorphically onto an open set) and $g : Y \to Z$ sc-smooth. items.title: Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47): $U \triangleleft F$, strong bundle maps and retractions

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47), p. 65 (preprint p. 48)
book.statement: $U \triangleleft F$ is $U \times F$ with the double filtration $U_m \oplus F_k$, $0 \le k \le m + 1$, and $(U \triangleleft F)[i]$ with levels $U_m \oplus F_{m+i}$. A strong bundle map $\Phi(u, h) = (\varphi(u), \Gamma(u, h))$, $\Gamma$ linear in $h$, preserves the double filtration and is sc-smooth $(U \triangleleft F)[i] \to (U' \triangleleft F')[i]$, $i = 0, 1$; a strong bundle retraction is one with $R \circ R = R$; $R(u, h) = (r(u), \Gamma(u, h))$ with $r$ an sc-smooth retraction.

lean.statement: $\Phi : E_0 \times F_0 \to E'_0 \times F'_0$ is a strong bundle map on $U \triangleleft F$ if it maps $U \times F$ into $U' \times F'$, its first component does not depend on $h$, its second is linear in $h$ for $u \in U$, it maps $U_m \oplus F_k$ into $U'_m \oplus F'_k$ for $k \le m + 1$, and it is sc-smooth on $U \times F_0$ for $E \oplus F$ and (through the lift of the fibre component to $F'_1$) on $U \times F_1$ for $E \oplus F^1$. A strong bundle retraction is one with $R \circ R = R$; its base $r(u) = R(u, 0)_1$ is an sc-smooth retraction on $U$, $\Gamma(u, \cdot)$ is a projection for $u \in O$, and $R$ is an sc-smooth retraction on $(U \triangleleft F)[0]$ and on $(U \triangleleft F)[1]$. $C \times F$ is a partial quadrant in $E \oplus F$ and $U \times F$ is relatively open in it.

diff: Sc-smoothness on $[1]$ is that of the induced map $U \oplus F_1 \to U' \oplus F'_1$; \"preserves the double filtration\" is read level by level.

Updated (2026-11-09): strong bundle isomorphisms are the project's `IsStrongBundleIso`, which is the text's wording, an invertible strong bundle map with strong bundle inverse (`exists_isStrongBundleIso_iff`), closed under identity, inverse and composition (gap G.14 closed). The remarks after the definition ($r$ a retraction, $\Gamma(u, \cdot)$ a projection) are the exposition's Lemma 5.A, proved here.

items.title: Definition 2.6.2 (preprint 2.48): local strong bundle retracts and $K[i]$

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.2 (preprint 2.48) and the remarks after it, pp. 65–67 (preprint pp. 49–50)
book.statement: A local strong bundle retract is $K = R(U \triangleleft F)$ for a strong bundle retraction, $p : K \to O$; $K_{m,k} = \{(u, h) \in O_m \oplus F_k : \Gamma(u, h) = h\}$, $K[i] = K_{0,i}$ with the filtration $K_{m,m+i}$; the projections $p : K[i] \to O$ are sc-smooth.

lean.statement: $K \subseteq E_0 \times F_0$ is a local strong bundle retract over $C$ if $K = R(U \times F_0)$ for a strong bundle retraction on some relatively open $U \subseteq C$; then $K = \{(u, h) : u \in O, \Gamma(u, h) = h\}$. Its double filtration $K_{m,k}$ and $K[1] = \{(u, h) \in E_0 \times F_1 : (u, h) \in K\}$ are defined level by level. $K$ is an sc-smooth retract in $(C \times F, E \oplus F)$ and $K[1]$ one in $(C \times F, E \oplus F^1)$, $K[1]$ being the image of $R$ on $(U \triangleleft F)[1]$; $p : K[i] \to O$ and the inclusion $K[1] \to K[0]$ are sc-smooth.

diff: $K[1]$ is a subset of $(E \oplus F^1)_0 = E_0 \times F_1$. The text's \"$p$ is sc-smooth\" is proved, with \"sc-smooth bundle map\" read as sc-smooth.
That $K[1]$ is the image of $R$ on $(U \triangleleft F)[1]$ uses that $R$ preserves the double filtration at $(m, k) = (0, 1)$ (exposition Lemma 5.B).

items.title: Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49): sections of a local strong bundle retract

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49), p. 66 (preprint p. 50)
book.statement: A section of $p : K \to O$ is $f : O \to K$ with $p \circ f = 1_O$; sc-smooth if it is sc-smooth into $K[0]$, sc⁺-smooth if sc-smooth into $K[1]$ (the text writes $K(0)$, $K(1)$); $f(x) = (x, \mathbf f(x))$ with the principal part $\mathbf f$.

lean.statement: An sc-smooth section is $f$ with $f(x)_1 = x$ on $O$ and $f$ sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ to $(K, C \times F, E \oplus F)$; an sc⁺-section is $f : E_0 \to E_0 \times F_1$ with $f(x)_1 = x$ on $O$, sc-smooth into $(K[1], C \times F, E \oplus F^1)$. An sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section.

diff: The principal part is not named separately; an sc⁺-section takes its fibre values in $F_1$ by type.

Updated (2026-11-09): the category $\mathcal{SBR}$ is `SBR`, its morphisms the maps $K \to K'$ with an extension that is fibrewise linear, preserves the double filtration and is sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$; strong bundle maps are morphisms and strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms (`IsStrongBundleMap.isHom`, `IsStrongBundleIso.toIso`). The functors $\mathrm{forget}[i]$, $i = 0, 1$, land in the category `ScRetr` of sc-smooth retracts, the bundle retracts $\mathcal{BR}$ of §2.1 not being formalized (gap G.5) (gap G.14 closed).

items.title: Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50): strong bundle charts, compatibility, atlases

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50), pp. 67–68 (preprint pp. 51–52)
book.statement: For $P : Y \to X$ (Y paracompact Hausdorff, fibres Banachable), a strong bundle chart $(\Phi, P^{-1}(V), K, U \triangleleft F)$: $K = R(U \triangleleft F)$, $V$ open with a homeomorphism $\varphi : V \to O$, $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K$ a homeomorphism covering $\varphi$, bounded linear on fibres. Charts are compatible if $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[i]$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, $i = 0, 1$; atlases and their equivalence.

lean.statement: A strong bundle chart consists of a chart $\varphi$ *of the M-polyfold $X$*, an sc-Banach space $F$, a strong bundle retraction $R$ on a relatively open $U \subseteq C$ whose base retract is $O$, and a homeomorphism $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K = R(U \times F_0)$ with $\Phi(y)_1 = \varphi(P(y))$, linear on each fibre $P^{-1}(x)$ (continuity on fibres follows). Two charts are compatible if $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$ and $\Phi \circ \Phi'^{-1}$ are sc-smooth between the overlap retracts on $[0]$ and, through the lift to $F_1$, on $[1]$, and map fibre components in $F_1$ to fibre components in $F'_1$. Atlases: pairwise compatible charts covering $Y$; equivalence: the union is an atlas. Equivalence of strong bundle atlases is an equivalence relation, and two atlases are equivalent iff every chart of one is compatible with every chart of the other; this rests on the locality of compatibility. A strong bundle chart restricts to every open $s \subseteq V$ (retraction domain $U \cap r^{-1}(W)$ for $\varphi(s) = O \cap W$, $K_s = \{(u, h) \in K \mid u \in \varphi(s)\}$, $\Phi$ unchanged), and restrictions of compatible charts are compatible.

diff: The base homeomorphism $\varphi$ is required to be a chart of $X$; the text asks only for a homeomorphism onto $O$, under which the strong bundle atlas would define its own structure on $X$.
\"Bounded linear on the fibres\" needs only linearity: continuity follows from $\Phi$ being a homeomorphism (`continuous_fiber`).
For $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ to be defined, the transition must map fibre components in $F_1$ to $F'_1$; the text takes this for granted, the definition states it.

The “equivalence class of strong bundle atlases” of Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) presupposes that the equivalence is transitive. It is: near a point of the overlap the transition $\Phi'' \circ \Phi^{-1}$ factors through a chart $\Phi'$ of the middle atlas, on $[0]$ and on $[1]$, and the $F_1$-condition passes through $\Phi'$; no continuity of $P$ is needed (Findings, Chapter 2, item 40). The restriction of a strong bundle chart to an open subset of the base, which the text uses silently (e.g. in Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2), V5.4), is formalized; a restriction whose retraction domain lies inside a given open $W \ni 0$ of $E$ is not, since $U \cap W$ need not be invariant under $r$ (item 42). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51): strong bundles; $Y[0]$, $Y[1]$, $P[0]$, $P[1]$ and $Y_{m,k}$

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) and the remarks after it, preprint p. 52
book.statement: A strong bundle over $X$ is $P : Y \to X$ (continuous surjection, $Y$ paracompact Hausdorff) with an equivalence class of strong bundle atlases. The charts induce a double filtration $Y_{m,k}$ and M-polyfolds $Y[i]$, $Y[i]_m = Y_{m,m+i}$; $P[i] : Y[i] \to X$ are sc-smooth.

lean.statement: A strong bundle is a continuous surjection $P : Y \to X$ ($Y$ Hausdorff paracompact) with Banachable fibres and a strong bundle atlas. The charts $\Phi$ form an sc-smooth atlas of $Y$, making it the M-polyfold $Y[0]$, and $P[0] : Y[0] \to X$ is sc-smooth. $Y_{m,k}$ ($k \le m + 1$) is defined by $\Phi(y) \in E_m \times F_k$ in all charts around $y$, and one chart suffices. $Y[1]$ is the set $Y_{0,1}$ with the topology generated by the charts $\Phi[1] : y \mapsto (\Phi(y)_1, \Phi(y)_2$ lifted to $F_1)$; these charts, onto the retracts $K[1]$, are pairwise compatible, their transition maps being the $[1]$-transitions, and make $Y[1]$ an M-polyfold; $P[1] : Y[1] \to X$ is sc-smooth. The charts of the strong bundle (`StrongBundle.IsChart`: compatible with the atlas) are those of the maximal atlas, which is equivalent to the given one: a chart is one iff it belongs to some atlas of the class, any two are compatible, restrictions of charts are charts, and equivalent atlases have the same charts.

chips: charts depend only on the class
diff: $Y[0]$ (the text's "the M-polyfold $Y$") and $Y[1]$ are constructed with the charts induced by the given atlas; the equivalence class of atlases is represented by one atlas, as for M-polyfolds. The notions defined through the charts compatible with the atlas therefore depend only on the class (`isChart_congr`, `isChart_iff_exists_equiv`; Findings, Chapter 2, item 43); those defined with the charts of the given atlas itself ($Y_{m,k}$, $Y[1]$ and its atlas, sc$^+$-sections) are not shown invariant. Updated in the third addendum of this page.

$Y[1]$ is the subset $Y_{0,1}$ with the topology generated by the sets $\Phi[1]^{-1}(W)$, as for $X_m$ in §2.3 (preprint §2.2); its paracompactness, required of an M-polyfold and not mentioned in the text, follows from metrizability (V2.64).

Chart independence of $Y_{m,k}$: for $k \le m$ it follows from the $[0]$-transition; for $k = m + 1$, and for the set $Y_{0,1}$ itself, it uses the condition that the $[1]$-transition carries fibre components in $F_1$ to $F'_1$, made explicit in Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) (V2.57).

items.title: Definition 2.6.6 (preprint 2.52): sections of a strong bundle

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.6 (preprint 2.52), p. 68 (preprint p. 53)
book.statement: A section is $f : X \to Y$ with $P \circ f = 1_X$; sc-smooth if sc-smooth into $Y[0]$, sc⁺ if sc-smooth into $Y[1]$.

lean.statement: A section is $f$ with $P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$; it is sc-smooth if it is sc-smooth $X \to Y[0]$ (Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14)); it is an sc⁺-section if in every strong bundle chart of the atlas its fibre values lie in $F_1$ and its representative $z \mapsto \Phi(f(\varphi^{-1}(z)))$, lifted to $E_0 \times F_1$, is sc-smooth from $O$ into $K[1]$. This holds iff $f$ is a section and $f = \iota \circ g$ for an sc-smooth $g : X \to Y[1]$, $\iota : Y[1] \to Y$ the inclusion.

chips: sc⁺ chart by chart = sc-smooth into $Y[1]$

items.title: Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53): the pull-back bundle

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53), p. 69 (preprint p. 53)
book.statement: For a strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and an sc-smooth $f : Z \to X$, $f^*Y = \{(z, y) : P(y) = f(z)\}$, $P_f(z, y) = z$, $P'(z, y) = y$, and $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$.

lean.statement: $f^*Y = \{(z, y) \in Z \times Y : P(y) = f(z)\}$ with $P_f$, $P'$ the projections; $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$; $P_f$ is continuous, and $f^*Y$ is closed in $Z \times Y$ when $X$ is Hausdorff and $P$, $f$ are continuous.

diff: As in the text, for any maps $P$, $f$.

items.title: Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54): the pull-back of a strong bundle is a strong bundle

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54), p. 69 (preprint p. 53)
book.statement: $P_f : f^*Y \to Z$ carries a natural structure of a strong bundle over $Z$ (\"the easy proof is left to the reader\").

lean.statement: For a strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and an sc-smooth $f : Z \to X$: $f^*Y$ is paracompact (it is metrizable, $Z$ and $Y[0]$ being metrizable by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16)), $P_f$ is a continuous surjection, its fibres $P_f^{-1}(z) \cong P^{-1}(f(z))$ are Banachable, and the pulled-back charts $\Phi_f(z, y) = (\psi(z), \mathrm{pr}_F\Phi(y))$, with the strong bundle retractions $R_g(w, h) = (r_Z(w), \Gamma(g(r_Z(w)), h))$, $g = \varphi \circ f \circ \psi^{-1}$, form a strong bundle atlas; so $P_f$ is a strong bundle with this atlas. Locally: $R_g$ is a strong bundle retraction with image $\{(w, h) : w \in O_Z, (g(w), h) \in K\}$; the transition maps of pulled-back charts are $(w, h) \mapsto (\psi_2\psi_1^{-1}(w), \mathrm{pr}_F(\Phi_2\Phi_1^{-1})(g_1(w), h))$, sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$.

diff: \"Natural structure\" is the atlas of all pulled-back charts; any two are compatible, so it involves no choice.
The paracompactness of $f^*Y$, required by Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) and not mentioned in the text, is proved from Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) for $Z$ and $Y[0]$.

“Natural” presumably also says that $P' : f^*Y \to Y$ is a strong bundle map (sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$); that is not formalized. In the charts $\Phi_f$, $\Phi$ it is $(w, h) \mapsto (g(w), h)$ on $K_g$ (Findings, Chapter 2, item 51; round-trip item V2.61). Recorded in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55): Smirnov's metrization theorem

book.label: §2.7.2 (preprint §2.6.2), Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55), p. 72 (preprint p. 56)
book.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space in which every point has a metrizable open neighbourhood is metrizable (quoted from Smirnov).

lean.statement: A paracompact Hausdorff space in which every point has a metrizable open neighbourhood is metrizable. More generally: a space $Y$ with open metrizable $V_i$ and a locally finite family of continuous $\rho_i \ge 0$, $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i \subseteq V_i$, not all zero at any point, is metrizable, with the metric $\sum_i |\rho_i(x) - \rho_i(y)| + \min(\rho_i(x), \rho_i(y)) \min(d_i(x, y), 1)$; and if $\pi : Y \to X$ is continuous into a paracompact Hausdorff $X$ and every point of $X$ has an open $U$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)$ metrizable, $Y$ is metrizable. Metrizable spaces are paracompact (Stone, from Mathlib).

diff: Quoted in the text; proved here (Mathlib does not have it), in the stronger pull-back form that Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) and Proposition 2.3.15(3) (preprint 2.19) use.

items.title: Restriction and locality of sc$^k$ maps

book.label: §§2.1, 2.3 (preprint §2.1–§2.2), used in Propositions 2.1.11, 2.3.1 (preprint 2.4, 2.10) and Definitions 2.3.4–2.3.8 (preprint 2.13–2.14), preprint p. 19
book.statement: Used without statement: an sc-smooth map restricted to a smaller relatively open set is sc-smooth (e.g. \"$r : U \to U \cap U'$ is sc-smooth\"), and sc-smoothness is a local property.

items.title: The space $Y[1]$ and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$

book.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), after Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51), p. 68 (preprint p. 52)
book.statement: Not stated: the text takes $Y[1]$ to be an M-polyfold on the set $Y_{0,1}$ without discussing its topology, its paracompactness or its inclusion into $Y[0]$.

With the topology generated by the charts $\Phi[1]$, the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y$ is continuous, so $Y[1]$ is Hausdorff; $Y[1]$ is metrizable, hence paracompact; and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is sc-smooth (in the charts it is $(u, h) \mapsto (u, \iota h)$).

items.title: Proposition 2.1.4: complete closed neighbourhoods in a retract

items.title: Definition 2.1.5: locally complete spaces

book.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.5, p. 23 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: A Hausdorff space $X$ is locally complete if every $x$ has open neighbourhoods $W(x)$, $V(x)$ such that $W(x)$ carries a metric inducing its topology, $V(x) \subseteq W(x)$, $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$, and $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ is complete for that metric.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2): classical smooth retractions have submanifold images
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2), p. 22 (preprint p. 18) (proof §2.7.1 (preprint §2.6.1), preprint pp. 54–55)
notFormalized.book: If $r : U \to U$ is a $C^\infty$ retraction of an open subset of a Banach space $E$, then $O = r(U)$ is a $C^\infty$ submanifold: near each $x \in O$ there are a splitting $E = R \oplus N$ and a diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ with $\psi(O \cap V) = R \cap W$ (the text prints $\psi(0) = x$ for $\psi(x) = 0$).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The proposition is classical and is used only as motivation (the contrast with sc-smooth retractions, whose images can change dimension). The exposition proves it in §8.1 with the inverse function theorem; its Lean version would need Mathlib's inverse function theorem for $C^\infty$ maps between Banach spaces and the splitting by the projection $Dr(0)$. Not attempted.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9): sc-smooth bundle retractions and bundle maps
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9), p. 29 (preprint p. 22)
notFormalized.book: A trivial sc-bundle $U \oplus F \to U$; an sc-smooth $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u, v))$, $\rho$ linear in $v$, $R \circ R = R$, is an sc-smooth bundle retraction with bundle retract $B = R(U \oplus F) \to O$; bundle maps $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u, v))$ with \"$p' \circ \Phi = p$\" (read $a \circ p$); the category $\mathcal{BR}$ and the functor $T : \mathcal R \to \mathcal{BR}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page, apart from the categories** (V2.92). Bundle retractions and bundle maps are defined by their shape, $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u)v)$ on $U \oplus F$ and $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u)v)$ with $\rho(u)$, $\phi(u)$ continuous linear, so $p' \circ \Phi = a \circ p$; $Tr$ is a bundle retraction covering $r^1$ and $Tf$ a bundle map covering $f^1$, and the transition maps of $TX$ are bundle maps (V2.94). Before, the tangent retraction $Tr$ (V2.8) and the strong bundle retractions of §2.6 (preprint §2.5) (V2.54) were the instances the theory used. The categories $\mathcal R$, $\mathcal{BR}$, $\mathcal{SBR}$ and their functors are still not formalized (Findings, Chapter 2, item 76).

notFormalized.title: $X_m$ as an M-polyfold for $m \ge 2$
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), after Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14), preprint p. 25
notFormalized.book: For every $m$, the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$ form an atlas on $X_m$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.93). For $m \ge 2$ the structure is the iterate $(X^1)^1 \cdots$. For every $m$ the identity of points is a homeomorphism $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$, and the level-$m$ lift of the level chart $\varphi^1$ is the level-$(m+1)$ lift of $\varphi$ (`MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, `MPolyfold.shift_level_eq`), so each iterate is $X_m$ with its topology and the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$. Since the fourth addendum the points were known to agree, $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (Findings, Chapter 5, items 142, 146). Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) is proved for every $X_m$ directly (V2.17); Proposition 2.3.17, $T(X^i) \equiv (TX)^i$, for every $i$ is V2.97 (Findings, Chapter 2, item 77).

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18): the linear structure of $T_xX$; Proposition 2.3.19 (3) (preprint 2.21) in $T_aX$
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18) and Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) (preprint 2.21), pp. 38–44 (preprint pp. 26–30)
notFormalized.book: $T_xX$ is a vector space with $\lambda[(x, \varphi, h_1)] + \mu[(x, \varphi, h_2)] = [(x, \varphi, \lambda h_1 + \mu h_2)]$, a Banach space through $T\varphi$, an sc-Banach space at smooth $x$; Proposition 2.3.19 (3) (preprint 2.21): $T_aA$ has an sc-complement in $T_aX$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.19, V2.21, V2.25). $T_xX$ is a vector space and for every chart $\varphi$ around $x$, $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_{\varphi(x)}O$ is a linear isomorphism and a homeomorphism onto the Banach space $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ (`tangentFiberLinearEquiv`, `tangentFiberContinuousLinearEquiv`), with the text's formula (`definition_2_3_14_2021`); the chart independence is the linearity of the fibre transitions, restrictions of $D(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})(\varphi(x))$. At a smooth $x$ the models $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ are sc-subspaces of $E$ with level-preserving transitions, so $T_xX$ is an sc-Banach space through any chart (`isScSubspace_tangentFiberModel`). Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) hold in $T_aX$, the sc-complement read through a chart (`proposition_2_3_19_3_linear_2021`, `proposition_2_3_19_3_sc_2021`, `proposition_2_3_19_4_2021`). Tangent maps of sc-smooth maps are continuous linear on the fibres (`theorem_2_3_16_linear_2021`). Statements elsewhere made in charts for want of this structure (V2.78, V2.99, Chapter 4, Chapter 9) are not restated with it.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19): $p : TX \to X_1$ is open
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19), p. 39 (preprint p. 27)
notFormalized.book: The projection $p : TX \to X_1$ is an open map.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.20). $p : TX \to X^1$ is open for every M-polyfold (`MPolyfold.isOpenMap_tangentProj`; Proposition 2.3.15 (2) in full, `proposition_2_3_15_two_2021`). The local step is the openness of $\mathrm{pr}_1 : TO \to O_1$, which the text states without proof: $o' \mapsto Tr(o', h) = (o', Dr(o')h)$ is continuous on $U_1$ since $Tr$ is $\mathrm{sc}^0$, and sends $o$ to $(o, h)$ (`ScRetraction.exists_isOpen_tangent_section`). This makes the field `isOpenMap_tangentProj` of Chapter 7's `MPolyfold.SmoothRegular` a theorem (V7.86) (Findings, Chapter 2, item 86).

notFormalized.title: Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28): $C_xO$ need not be a partial quadrant
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28), p. 47 (preprint p. 33)
notFormalized.book: Naively one might expect $C_xO$ to be a partial quadrant in $T_xO$; \"however, this is in general not the case\".
notFormalized.instead: **Settled since the first edition of this page, in the negative** (third addendum; V2.33): the claim is false. At every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract, tame or not, $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ (with the sc-structure induced from $E$), of dimension $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_C(x)$; the proof reduces it to Flor's theorem on nonnegative idempotent matrices, proved in the needed case. For a non-tame retract only the equality of that dimension with $d_C(x)$ can fail (Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31)). The text gives no example, and none exists (Findings, Chapter 2, item 50).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29): $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ through sc-smooth paths; $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29), pp. 48–49 (preprint pp. 33–35)
notFormalized.book: For a retract and a smooth $x \in O$: (1) $T^R_xO$ is the closure of the derivatives $\dot\alpha(0)$ of sc-smooth paths $\alpha : (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \to O$ through $x$; (2) $C_xO$ the closure of the one-sided derivatives of sc-smooth paths $\alpha : [0, \varepsilon) \to O$; (3) $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized in the path formulation.** Sc-smooth paths would need the constant sc-structure on an interval as a retract and the density of smooth points of $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ (the exposition's Lemma 3.A on all levels). The sign arguments that the proof consists of are formalized (V2.34), and Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30) is proved from them, not from the lemma. (3) is not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), second statement: equality makes $C_xO$ a partial quadrant
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), p. 50 (preprint p. 35) (second statement)
notFormalized.book: If $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x)$, then $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V2.33, V2.37), without the hypothesis: $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ at every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract, whatever $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$ is, and the quadrant has dimension $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$, which is $d_O(x)$ under the hypothesis. The sc-Banach structure of $T_xO$ and $T^R_xO$ as an sc-subspace, which the exposition supplied on paper, are proved without tameness; the smooth lifts come from the columns given by Flor's theorem (V2.33).

notFormalized.title: The extended faces of a partial quadrant, intrinsically
notFormalized.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), preprint p. 39
notFormalized.book: $\{e \in C : d_C(e) = 1\}$ has exactly $k$ connected components $A_i$; each lies in a smallest subspace $f_i$ (an extended face), with a half-space $H_{f_i} \supset C$; $\mathcal F(e) = \{f : e \in f\}$ and $d_C(e) = \#\mathcal F(e)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized as stated.** The formalization works with a presentation $T$ of $C$ and takes the coordinate hyperplanes $f_i = \{\lambda_i = 0\}$ as the extended faces (`coordHyper`); that a connected piece of $\{d_C = 1\}$ lies in one $f_i$ is `subset_coordHyper_of_isPreconnected` (V2.45). That $E_x$ does not depend on the presentation is proved (`minimalSubspaceWith_eq`, V2.39); the count of components, the minimality of $f_i$ and the intrinsic description of the extended faces are not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38): $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ of an M-polyfold
notFormalized.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38), p. 57 (preprint p. 42)
notFormalized.book: For a smooth $x \in X$, $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ are the preimages of $T^R_oO$ and $C_oO$ under $T\psi(x)$ for any chart $\psi$; well defined by Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30). For tame $X$, $C_xX$ is a partial quadrant and $d_X(x) = \dim(T_xX/T^R_xX) = d_{C_xX}(0_x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized in part since the first edition of this page.** With the linear structure of $T_xX$ (G.7, closed), $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ are defined in $T_xX$ as the preimages under $T\varphi(x)$ of $T^R_{\varphi(x)}O$ and $C_{\varphi(x)}O$, for a chart and a presentation of its partial quadrant (`reducedTangentFiber`, `partialConeFiber`), and they do not depend on the chart or the presentation, at every $x \in X_1$ (`reducedTangentFiber_eq`, `partialConeFiber_eq`, by Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30)); in a tame chart at a smooth $x$, $d_X(x) = \dim(T_xX/T^R_xX)$ (`finrank_quotient_reducedTangentFiber_eq_degIndex`). **Not formalized**: that $C_xX$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xX$ and $d_{C_xX}(0_x) = d_X(x)$; in a chart this is V2.42 (`proposition_2_36_partialCone`). The local forms are V2.32, V2.35.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47): strong bundle isomorphisms; the category $\mathcal{SBR}$
notFormalized.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47) and after Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49), pp. 65–67 (preprint pp. 48–51)
notFormalized.book: A strong bundle isomorphism is an invertible strong bundle map with strong bundle inverse. The category $\mathcal{SBR}$ of local strong bundle retracts and the functors $\mathrm{forget}[i] : \mathcal{SBR} \to \mathcal{BR}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.54, V2.56).
